To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of 5% zirconia- impregnated PMMA did not significantly improve flexural strength of the denture base material.
the flexural strength properties of HI PMMA dentures were improved by the addition of zirconia nanofillers at two different concentrations (3 and 5 wt.%).
the addition of zirconia nanoparticle to HI heat-polymeric PMMA resin can significantly enhance the equivalent flexural strength, but not the impact resistance, of the dentures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of complete removable denture specimens from HI heat-poly-merised PMMA with and without zirconia nanoparticles.
the development of novel denture materials with improved flexural strength properties for clinical applications.
the development of a new denture material with improved mechanical properties, which is a very important aspect in the field of prosthodontics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of HI heat-plymerised PMMA with 5 wt% of zirconia particles is not suitable as a denture material.

the use of 5 wt.% of zirconia in the manufacture of PMMA-based dentures does not improve the mechanical strength and the application of fatigue cycling did not significantly improve their mechanical strength.
the use of HI PMMA reinforced with zirconium nanoparticles is not recommended for denture base fabrication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
zirconia nanoparticles are not suitable for reinforcing HI heat-poly-merised PMMA for denture fabrication.
the addition of zirconia to the HI PMMA dentures does not improve their flexural strength.
the use of HI heat-ploymerised PMMA in the fabrication of dentures is not a suitable option.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the application of fatigue cycling loading does not significantly improve the flexural strength properties of denture specimens.
the flexural strength properties of HI PMMA resin reinforced by zirconia nanoparticles do not significantly improve the flexural properties of denture base resin.
the use of HI heat-curing PMMA resin reinforced by zirconia nanoparticles can improve the equivalent flexual strength of denture bases.
